title: Orca AI and NorthStandard report 52% fewer high-severity close encounters across 139 vessels during their first year with the system
summary: Orca AI and NorthStandard report 52% fewer severe close encounters across 139 vessels of several types, comparing early and late use without an untreated fleet.
account: The Maritime Executive reported on 12 March 2024 that NorthStandard helps pay for its members to install and use Orca AI. Trade reports published on 15 and 16 April 2026 describe a study by the protection and indemnity insurer NorthStandard with Orca AI. The reports are MarineLink, Riviera Maritime Media's Martyn Wingrove, and Hellenic Shipping News reproducing Orca AI's release. The study covered a globally operating cohort of 139 vessels of several types fitted with Orca AI's navigation platform. Riviera Maritime Media described the cohort as 139 container vessels. The report states that its data were collected between 2023 and 2025. Across more than 10.8 million nautical miles, the study compared the first three months after installation with months 10 to 12. It reported a 52% reduction in high-severity close encounters, with 22% within the first six months. The reduction was 36% in the North and Baltic Seas and 18% in the seas around China and Japan. Encounters were defined by closest point of approach, time to closest point of approach, interactions under the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs) and traffic density. Orca AI's report page states that such encounters declined from 2.7 per vessel per month early after implementation to 1.3 by months 10 to 12. NorthStandard's head of loss prevention Colin Gillespie and Orca AI's chief executive Yarden Gross are quoted. The design is a before-and-after comparison on the same vessels with no control fleet, and the report is hosted by the vendor. Because NorthStandard subsidizes its members' use of Orca AI, the insurer that co-wrote the 2026 study has a financial stake in the system.

display.answer: MarineLink, Riviera Maritime Media and Hellenic Shipping News report the joint study. Hellenic Shipping News reproduces Orca AI's release. The OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor entry relays the same 52% figure. All these figures trace to the joint report, which Orca AI hosts. The Maritime Executive reported in March 2024 that NorthStandard subsidizes its members' use of Orca AI.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Orca AI and NorthStandard report 52% fewer severe close encounters across 139 vessels of several types, comparing early and late use without an untreated fleet.
fields.account: The Maritime Executive reported on 12 March 2024 that NorthStandard helps pay for its members to install and use Orca AI. Trade reports published on 15 and 16 April 2026 describe a study by the protection and indemnity insurer NorthStandard with Orca AI. The reports are MarineLink, Riviera Maritime Media's Martyn Wingrove, and Hellenic Shipping News reproducing Orca AI's release. The study covered a globally operating cohort of 139 vessels of several types fitted with Orca AI's navigation platform. Riviera Maritime Media described the cohort as 139 container vessels. The report states that its data were collected between 2023 and 2025. Across more than 10.8 million nautical miles, the study compared the first three months after installation with months 10 to 12. It reported a 52% reduction in high-severity close encounters, with 22% within the first six months. The reduction was 36% in the North and Baltic Seas and 18% in the seas around China and Japan. Encounters were defined by closest point of approach, time to closest point of approach, interactions under the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs) and traffic density. Orca AI's report page states that such encounters declined from 2.7 per vessel per month early after implementation to 1.3 by months 10 to 12. NorthStandard's head of loss prevention Colin Gillespie and Orca AI's chief executive Yarden Gross are quoted. The design is a before-and-after comparison on the same vessels with no control fleet, and the report is hosted by the vendor. Because NorthStandard subsidizes its members' use of Orca AI, the insurer that co-wrote the 2026 study has a financial stake in the system.
